source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting excessive industrial emissions in an air-quality report

1. Start with the monitoring records.
2.
completion:
Follow the methodology specified in the relevant national or international air-quality standards.
3. Measure emissions data accurately using calibrated equipment.
4. Collect sufficient data to ensure robust analysis.
5. Note all the parameters measured (e.g., PM10, PM2.5, NOx, SOx, VOCs, CO, CO2).
6. Record the date, time, location, and weather conditions during data collection.
7. Ensure the report includes information about the source, type, and volume of emissions.
8. Be specific about the identifying features of the emitters (e.g., industrial stack, fugitive emissions).
9. Use statistical methods to analyze data and highlight any exceedance of standards.
10. Include a detailed description of any unusual events or incidents.
11. Use GIS or mapping software to illustrate spatial patterns of pollution, if possible.
12. Compare the data with historical data and report any trends.
13. Identify any component of the emissions
